notes.title: Open hands and closed ones
notes.science: In a trust game, a creature that always shares does well among sharers and badly against a keeper. Krit takes the berry and gives nothing back.
notes.limits: The game here has only two moves, share or keep, with the same payoff every time.
notes.counter: One meeting says little. Over many meetings, a keeper can run out of creatures who will share with it.
notes.question: Can Pim stay open after meeting Krit?

sources.label: The Evolution of Trust, Nicky Case
The Evolution of Cooperation, Axelrod and Hamilton, 1981

notes.title: Mistakes happen
notes.science: Sometimes a gift fails to arrive, or it arrives and looks like something else. In a long game, one mistake can start a feud between two fair creatures.
notes.limits: Here the chance of a mistake is one number, set by hand.
notes.counter: Real misreadings are rarely random. They follow fear, history, and who is watching.
notes.question: How much forgiveness does a mistake call for?

sources.label: The Evolution of Trust, Nicky Case
How to Cope with Noise in the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma, Wu and Axelrod, 1995
